analysis.title: The long trade got harder, the hedge got cheaper
key_insights: Since August 27, the S&P 500 is up 1.3% while the S&P excluding the AI names is down more than 5% (GS). The gap is close to the widest since the AI trade began in early 2023, so AI is holding the index together.
GS Prime data shows Mag 7 exposure at about 22% of total US exposure, the highest since their data began in 2022. AI is no longer an uncrowded trade.
Tech was the only US sector net bought by hedge funds in September, with the largest monthly buying since February 2025.
Rates have repriced sharply and oil remains elevated, and large parts of the real economy have taken the hit. The mega-cap AI complex largely has not.
Two paths: macro turns friendlier and the market broadens out, or rates and oil stay difficult and start to hurt the parts of the market that have so far been immune.
Crowding is local. GS has US fundamental long/short net exposure at the 2nd percentile over five years, so overall equity positioning is light and should cushion meaningful dips.

GS argues a friendlier macro backdrop would unlock the most upside in areas left behind (housing, middle-income consumer, macro-sensitive pockets) where positioning and multiples are depressed. Lower rates could mean breadth rather than more AI.
Equity vol has collapsed despite a harder macro backdrop and more concentrated leadership, so protection is cheaper. Investors who want to stay long do not need to sell the upside to afford hedges.

sector_views.rationale: Only US sector net bought by hedge funds in September, and Mag 7 exposure is at a record share of US exposure, so the AI trade is now crowded.
GS argues positioning and multiples are depressed, so a friendlier macro backdrop would unlock the biggest upside here.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher rates are a headwind for the parts of the real economy that have already taken the hit and could eventually weigh on mega-cap AI.
Elevated oil adds to macro pressure on the real economy and is a risk to the AI-led market if it persists.

trade_ideas.description: Stay long equities and buy cheap protection (hedges) instead of selling upside
trade_ideas.rationale: Equity vol has collapsed while the macro backdrop is harder and positioning in the winners is fuller, so hedges cost less.
trade_ideas.risk: Rates and oil stay difficult and start to hit the mega-cap AI complex.

risk_factors: Rates and oil staying high could eventually hit the mega-cap AI stocks that have so far been immune.
Index concentration: the S&P ex-AI is down more than 5% since August 27, so the index depends on AI names.
Crowding in Mag 7 and tech after record exposure and heavy September hedge fund buying.
vol_and_positioning: Equity vol has collapsed even as the macro backdrop worsened and leadership concentrated, which makes protection cheap.
Mag 7 exposure is about 22% of total US exposure, the highest since 2022 (GS Prime).
US fundamental long/short net exposure is in the 2nd percentile over five years (GS), so crowding sits in AI winners while the broad market is under-positioned.
Hedge funds net bought tech in September, the largest monthly buying since February 2025.
Suggested stance: stay long while protection is cheap rather than selling the upside.
